## Goal
- Reconcile all valid workspace updates into an owner-controlled GitHub branch, test, commit, deploy from the final owner SHA, build the matching APK, and collect production/device/autonomous-operation proof.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Start with Phase 1 and Batch 1; do not edit owner `main` directly.
- Use a clean owner-controlled clone and branch `reconcile/final-ivx-owner-control`.
- Create safety tag `pre-final-reconciliation-YYYYMMDD-HHMM` before reconciliation.
- Process at most five functional files per batch in the mandated Batch 1–5 order.
- Preserve newer valid owner production fixes and valid workspace behavior through surgical/manual merges.
- Remove obsolete Rork runtime references; do not permanently delete historical material.
- Add focused regressions and run tests before advancing each batch.
- Commit only passed batches with mandated commit messages.
- Deploy only after all selected merges and full clean-clone test gate pass.
- Do not claim deployment, APK, device QA, autonomous proof, or owner-control parity without exact evidence and matching SHAs.
- Required bilingual routing coverage includes:
  - `Can you create an app from scratch?`
  - `Can you create a new module?`
  - `Fix owner login.`
  - `Deploy this change.`
  - `How many active properties?`
  - Spanish equivalents.

## Progress
### Done
- Step 1 candidate inventory and Step 2 reconciliation planning were completed:
  - `audit/reconciliation-matrix.json`
  - `audit/reconciliation-matrix.md`
  - `audit/reconciliation-summary.md`
- Matrix totals:
  - `KEEP_GITHUB`: 4
  - `KEEP_WORKSPACE`: 2
  - `MERGE_MANUALLY`: 25
  - `IGNORE_GENERATED`: 5
  - `ARCHIVE_OBSOLETE`: 19
  - `BLOCK_SECRET`: 0
  - `NEEDS_OWNER_DECISION`: 7
- Owner baseline and production baseline identified as:
  - repository: `ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform`
  - branch: `main`
  - SHA: `d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7`
- `/tmp/ivx-owner-audit` was verified as an owner GitHub clone:
  - branch: `main`
  - HEAD: `d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7`
  - origin repository: `https://github.com/ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform.git`
  - clean working tree
  - zero gitlinks
  - zero submodules.
- Read `.rork/skills/platforms/SKILL.md`; no app-creation action is relevant.
- Prior Batch 1 assessment found `expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx` is the only demonstrated substantive same-path workspace-vs-owner functional difference among initially reviewed candidates.
- `expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx` diff was inspected:
  - workspace imports `shouldStartAssistantBeforePersistence`
  - local-first `send_and_ai` / `ai_only` can trigger the assistant before `sendQueue.mutateAsync` completes
  - send-only, attachment, and remote-first behavior stays persistence-first.
- Other initially reviewed candidates were non-functional:
  - `backend/api/ivx-autonomy.ts`: comment-only environment variable name.
  - `backend/api/ivx-autonomous-runs.ts`: final newline only.
  - `backend/api/ivx-autonomous-task-engine-api.ts`: final newline only.

### In Progress
- Validate the clean owner baseline and define the final Batch 1 set of at most five functional files.
- Inspect existing owner routing/context behavior for all mandated English and Spanish prompts.
- Determine focused test additions for:
  - engineering intent selection
  - property/business-data intent selection

### Blocked

- Exact required bilingual acceptance prompts have no discovered single dedicated regression suite:
  - grep for `classifyOwnerActionTypeWithContext|How many active|Cuántas.*activas|propiedades activas` in `backend` tests returned no matches.

- Treat `/tmp/ivx-owner-audit` at `d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7` as the clean owner-controlled reconciliation base.

- 8. Continue Batch 2 only after Batch 1 passes; do not merge to `main` or deploy before Phases 2–5 are complete.

2|name: platforms
     3|description: Use this skill whenever the user asks to create, scaffold, add, or
     4|  set up an app in the current Rork workspace, including requests like "create
     5|  an iOS app for this website" or adding a native iOS/Swift, Android/Kotlin,
     6|  Expo/React Native, or web app alongside an existing app. This unlocks the
     7|  createApp tool; do not reject app-creation requests just because another app
     8|  already exists.
     9|---
    10|
    11|### createApp
    12|
    13|Create a new app inside the workspace. Writes template files into a subfolder and
    14|creates/updates the root rork.json manifest.
    15|
    16|When to call:
    17|- Empty workspace: you MUST call this before writing any code.
    18|- Existing workspace: call when the user asks to add another app (e.g. an iOS app alongside an
    19|  existing web app).
    20|
    21|Picking `framework` for the FIRST app:
    22|- Default to the user's selected platform (named in the new-project nudge).
    23|- Override only on clear intent for another platform — by name OR by use:
    24|  iPhone/iPad/App Store/widget → `swift`; Android/Play Store → `kotlin`;
    25|  website/dashboard/"deploy to my domain"/runs in a browser → `web`. Intent need not be the
    26|  exact word ("deploy it to my domain" → `web`); the app's genre alone is not intent (a
    27|  "CS2-style FPS is a PC game" stays on the selected platform).
    28|- createApp rejects the first attempt whose `framework` differs from the selected platform.
    29|  If the user really did ask for the other platform, just call createApp again with the same
    30|  `framework` and it goes through; otherwise switch to the selected platform.
    31|- `react-native` is only valid when the project was originally started with React Native;
    32|  the call is rejected otherwise. React native is deprecated and will be removed in the future.
    33|- Swift 3D games / RealityKit games → `swift`. Decide orientation from the requested genre,
    34|  camera, and controls before creating the app.
    35|- Use `swiftTemplateProfile: "landscape-3d-game"` when the chosen orientation is landscape:
    36|  explicit landscape/horizontal requests, generic or ambiguous Swift/RealityKit 3D games,
    37|  racing/driving/flight, FPS/TPS/shooters, arena combat, action RPG/open-world/adventure,
    38|  sports/fighting, dual-stick controls, wide tactical maps, or designs that need a wide
    39|  camera view or two-thumb controls.
    40|- Do not use the landscape profile for portrait-first games: endless/lane runners, vertical
    41|  runners/climbers/fallers, one-tap or swipe hypercasual games, idle/merge/tycoon/collection
    42|  games, card/board/puzzle/gacha games, vertical shooters, rhythm lane games, regular apps,
    43|  AR/model viewers, or non-game 3D showcases.
    44|
    45|Ask the user for a clear app name/alias, then call this tool with the name and framework.
    46|If a Swift/RealityKit 3D game's orientation is ambiguous, default to landscape and include
    47|`swiftTemplateProfile`; do not stop to ask the user. Omit the profile when the user
    48|explicitly requests portrait/vertical or the prompt clearly matches a portrait-first genre.
    49|The repo folder path is derived automatically from that name, for example `ios-client-demo`,
    50|`android-field-team`, or `web-marketing-site`.
    51|
    52|Temporary rollout constraint: only one app per framework can be created right now. If the
    53|project already has an iOS, Android, or Web app, do not create another one of that same

    55|
    56|```json
    57|{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":60,"description":"Display name for the app (e.g. 'My Fitness Tracker')"},"framework":{"type":"string","enum":["react-native","swift","kotlin","web"],"description":"Framework to use"},"path":{"description":"Exact app folder path to create. 2|name: backend
     3|description: Add server-side capabilities to a Rork project — including
     4|  Supabase, Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, realtime/multiplayer, webhooks,
     5|  scheduled tasks, and edge functions. Routes between Cloudflare-first and
     6|  Supabase-first internally.
     7|aliases:
     8|  - server
     9|  - api
    10|  - webhook
    11|  - realtime
    12|  - multiplayer
    13|  - database
    14|  - persistence
    15|  - durable object
    16|  - worker
    17|  - supabase
    18|---
    19|
    20|# Backend
    21|
    22|Use this skill for backend work in Rork projects. There are two modern services and one legacy stack:
    23|
    24|- **Cloudflare Workers + Durable Objects** — portable server-side code, realtime connection handling, and scoped durable SQLite storage. This is the default for APIs, webhooks, business logic, validation, third-party integrations, scheduled tasks, realtime, multiplayer, and per-room/per-project state. Read .rork/skills/backend/cloudflare/overview.md.
    25|- **Supabase Postgres** — managed relational SQL storage with Row Level Security. Use it when the app needs global relational queries, RLS-protected client access, reporting, or data that should not be partitioned by Durable Object identity. Read .rork/skills/backend/supabase/overview.md.
    26|- **Legacy Hono + tRPC** — only for projects that already have `backend/hono.ts`. Read .rork/skills/backend/legacy-hono/overview.md.
    27|
    28|
    29|## Default to Cloudflare for Code
    30|
    31|If you are adding any server-side code, prefer Cloudflare Workers. The Worker is vanilla Cloudflare (`export default { fetch }`) and can be lifted into a normal Cloudflare account with a `wrangler.jsonc` if the project ever needs to migrate off Rork. That portability also makes future bug fixes and backwards-compatible API evolution easier: the code owns the API boundary instead of spreading behavior across client calls and database policies.
    32|
    33|Use Cloudflare for:
    34|
    35|- API endpoints called by React Native, Swift, or web apps.
    36|- Webhook handlers (Stripe, Resend, GitHub, etc.).
    37|- Business logic, validation, permissions beyond simple row ownership, third-party API calls, and response shaping.
    38|- Realtime, multiplayer, chat, presence, collaborative state, WebSockets, and scheduled tasks via Durable Objects.
    39|- Durable Object storage when the data naturally belongs to one room, one match, one user session, one document, or one project-scoped actor.
    40|
    41|
    42|## Choose the Data Layer
    43|
    44|Cloudflare can be the database too. Durable Objects include per-object SQLite storage (`this.ctx.storage.sql`), so a Worker can own both the API and the durable state without adding Supabase.
    45|
    46|Use **Durable Object storage** when:
    47|
    48|- The app needs multiplayer rooms, presence, chat, matchmaking, collaborative documents, or any WebSocket fanout.
    49|- State is naturally scoped to a stable id such as `roomId`, `matchId`, `documentId`, `userId`, or `projectId`.
    50|- You want one colocated authority for connections plus data: the DO handles sockets, writes SQLite rows, runs periodic timers, and serves reads.
    51|- The data is small to medium, local to that object, and does not need global SQL joins across every project/user.
    52|
    53|
    54|Use **Supabase Postgres** when:
    55|
    56|- The app needs global relational queries, cross-user reporting, search/filtering across many records, SQL joins, or admin analytics.
    57|- The client should read/write directly with Row Level Security.
    58|- The data should live in one central relational database instead of being partitioned across Durable Object instances.
    59|
    60|
    61|Common patterns:
    62|
    63|1. **Cloudflare Worker + Durable Object storage** (default for realtime and scoped state). The Worker/DO owns both API and data.
    64|2. **Cloudflare Worker -> Supabase** (recommended for non-trivial logic over relational data). The Worker owns the public API and calls Supabase as the database.
    65|3. **Client -> Supabase directly with RLS** (acceptable for thin CRUD like TODOs, profile editing, simple user-owned records). RLS guards rows, and there is little or no custom server-side behavior.
    66|
    67|
    68|Move from direct client access to a Worker-owned API as soon as business logic grows. RLS is useful, but it is Supabase-specific; portable behavior belongs in Cloudflare code when possible.
    69|
    70|## Edge Function Choice
    71|
    72|Prefer Cloudflare Workers over Supabase Edge Functions. Use Supabase Edge Functions only when the function must run inside Supabase's environment with elevated database privileges or Supabase-specific auth context. For normal APIs and integrations, use Cloudflare.
    73|
    74|## Existing Projects
    75|
    76|Never migrate an existing Supabase-based project to Cloudflare just because Cloudflare is the default for new code. Continue the existing architecture unless the user explicitly asks for migration. The portability principle is for choosing where to put new behavior, not for creating churn.
    77|
    78|For legacy `backend/hono.ts` projects, extend the existing stack unless the user explicitly asks to migrate.

(End of file - total 78 lines)

2|name: debugging
     3|description: Playbooks and the `rork-agent logs` CLI for investigating runtime
     4|  logs, behavioral runtime failures, App Store build failures, backend issues,
     5|  and Supabase logs. Use this skill when troubleshooting crashes, logs, broken
     6|  app behavior, UI not updating, or deployment problems.
     7|aliases:
     8|  - runtime logs
     9|  - runtime behavior
    10|  - crash logs
    11|  - app logs
    12|  - build logs
    13|  - doesn't work
    14|  - does not work
    15|  - still broken
    16|  - nothing happens
    17|  - button does nothing
    18|  - ui not updating
    19|  - not updating
    20|  - still the same
    21|  - tap does nothing
    22|  - screen does not change
    23|  - app store build failure
    24|  - supabase logs
    25|  - edge function logs
    26|  - investigate error
    27|---
    28|
    29|# Debugging Skill
    30|
    31|Playbooks plus the `rork-agent logs` CLI for debugging issues in your Rork app.
    32|
    33|## Which Playbook To Read
    34|
    35|- Behavior is wrong but the app builds and runs: read runtime-behavior-debugging.md before editing again. Use this for vague feedback like "it doesn't work", "still broken", "nothing happens", "button does nothing", "the tap does nothing", "not updating", "still the same", or "the screen does not change".
    36|- Runtime logs, crashes, or user-flow tracing: read runtime-logs.md.
    37|- Build, bundle, compile, archive, or App Store build failures: read build-error-debugging.md.
    38|- Backend, deployment, or Supabase failures: fetch logs with the CLI below, then apply the relevant playbook.
    39|
    40|
    41|## Fetching logs: `rork-agent logs <source>`
    42|
    43|Run in the bash tool. Output is one log per line, so pipe it to rg / head / jq to filter:
    44|
    45|```bash
    46|rork-agent logs runtime --errors | rg -i "network"   # app runtime logs, errors only
    47|rork-agent logs backend --limit 100                   # Deno hosting (Freestyle) logs
    48|rork-agent logs appstore                              # App Store build errors
    49|rork-agent logs ai-gateway --message-id <id>          # failed AI model API calls
    50|rork-agent logs supabase --since 2026-01-15T00:00:00Z # Supabase edge/postgres/auth logs
    51|```
    52|
    53|Sources:
    54|
    55|- runtime — logs from the live app (console output, crashes). Newest first; page back with `--before <id>`.
    56|- backend — Deno hosting logs from Freestyle (deployment logs, server errors).
    57|- appstore — App Store build errors and failure reasons.
    58|- ai-gateway — AI model API responses (OpenAI/Anthropic/Bedrock via the gateway); defaults to failures.
    59|- supabase — Supabase project logs (edge functions, postgres, auth, realtime). Requires a provisioned Supabase backend. Supports `--sql`, `--since`, `--until`.
    60|
    61|
    62|All sources are scoped to the current project automatically. See runtime-logs.md for the full flag reference and paging workflow.

(End of file - total 62 lines)
